old_value: {"id":"project-LICHEN-worker6-xvqs","title":"Spec: bind x5chain to COSE kid and fix 8.13 signing model","description":"Pre-existing gap in spec/06-security.md §8.13 verification (surfaced by viku.1 codereview, kimi-k3): when an x5chain is present, §8.13 Verification steps (lines ~1088-1097) never require the chain end-entity key to be the key that verifies the COSE_Sign1 signature, never bind the chain to the COSE kid (issuer-iid) — so a hostile node holding ANY chain from ANY configured anchor can present credentials with an arbitrary issuer IID, defeating issuer-based policy and poisoning per-issuer seq caches. Also unresolved: (a) the COSE alg is fixed to -65537 Schnorr48-Ed25519 (node key) while §8.13.2 use cases (identity name/email, organizational role) read as CA-asserted claims — if the node signs with its own key and merely carries a CA chain, payload claims are self-asserted; the spec must state which key signs and what the CA's signature actually attests; (b) payload subject-iid (claim key 1) is bound only to the presenting node (step 5), not to the x5chain leaf SAN — claim/certificate mix-and-match is unaddressed. Needs a coherent statement: e.g. leaf key verifies COSE signature AND derived IID == kid == payload subject-iid == leaf SAN IID, plus what role CA signatures play.
